anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet, the SPDT slide switch S1 (1825232-1) has its two outer pins wired to the signals: pin 1 (MH1) → HW_RESET and pin 3 (MH2) → GND, while the middle pin 2 (the switch pole/common) carries a no-connect (X) marker and is left floating.
anomalies.expected: The specification's reference netlist wires the switch as pin1→GND and pin2→HW_RESET (the pole on HW_RESET, one throw on GND), so that actuating the slide connects HW_RESET to GND and resets the SKW92A. The drawing instead connects the two throws and leaves the pole open, so no switch position ever joins HW_RESET to GND.

evidence.quote: S1 1825232-1: pin 1 (MH1) wire → HW_RESET, pin 3 (MH2) wire → GND, pin 2 stub terminated with a no-connect 'X' (EthernetAndPower.kicad_sch, image 7, top-right)
netlist: pin1→GND, pin2→HW_RESET (SKW92A pin 45) ... S1.1→GND, S1.2→HW_RESET→SKW92A pin 45 HW_RESET

anomalies.impact: The hardware reset button is non-functional: because the SPDT common (pin 2) is unconnected, sliding S1 never pulls the HW_RESET line to GND, so the user cannot reset the module via the physical switch.

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the reference at the reset switch S1: the schematic ties HW_RESET and GND to the two throw pins (1 and 3) and leaves the common/pole pin (2) no-connected, whereas the spec's netlist uses pin1→GND and pin2→HW_RESET. With the pole floating, the SPDT slide switch can never connect HW_RESET to GND, so the reset button does not work.
